verses.text: Listen, islands, to me. Listen, you peoples, from afar: Yahweh has called me from the womb; from the inside of my mother he has mentioned my name.
He has made my mouth like a sharp sword. He has hidden me in the shadow of his hand. He has made me a polished shaft. He has kept me close in his quiver.
He said to me, “You are my servant; Israel, in whom I will be glorified.”
But I said, “I have labored in vain. I have spent my strength in vain for nothing; yet surely the justice due to me is with Yahweh, and my reward with my God.”
Now Yahweh says, he who formed me from the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob again to him, and to gather Israel to him, for I am honorable in Yahweh’s eyes, and my God has become my strength.

Indeed, he says, “It is too light a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel? I will also give you as a light to the nations, that you may be my salvation to the end of the earth.”

Yahweh, the Redeemer of Israel, and his Holy One, says to him whom man despises, to him whom the nation abhors, to a servant of rulers: “Kings shall see and rise up; princes, and they shall worship; because of Yahweh who is faithful, even the Holy One of Israel, who has chosen you.”

Yahweh says, “In an acceptable time I have answered you, and in a day of salvation I have helped you. I will preserve you, and give you for a covenant of the people, to raise up the land, to make them inherit the desolate heritage:
saying to those who are bound, ‘Come out!’; to those who are in darkness, ‘Show yourselves!’ “They shall feed along the paths, and their pasture shall be on all treeless heights.
They shall not hunger nor thirst; neither shall the heat nor sun strike them: for he who has mercy on them will lead them. He will guide them by springs of water.
I will make all my mountains a road, and my highways shall be exalted.
Behold, these shall come from afar; and behold, these from the north and from the west; and these from the land of Sinim.”
Sing, heavens; and be joyful, earth; and break out into singing, mountains: for Yahweh has comforted his people, and will have compassion on his afflicted.
But Zion said, “Yahweh has forsaken me, and the Lord has forgotten me.”
“Can a woman forget her nursing child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? Yes, these may forget, yet I will not forget you!
Behold, I have engraved you on the palms of my hands. your walls are continually before me.
Your children hurry. Your destroyers and those who devastated you will leave you.

Lift up your eyes all around, and see: all these gather themselves together, and come to you. As I live,” says Yahweh, “you shall surely clothe yourself with them all as with an ornament, and dress yourself with them, like a bride.
“For, as for your waste and your desolate places, and your land that has been destroyed, surely now that land will be too small for the inhabitants, and those who swallowed you up will be far away.
The children of your bereavement will say in your ears, ‘This place is too small for me. Give me a place to live in.’

Then you will say in your heart, ‘Who has conceived these for me, since I have been bereaved of my children, and am solitary, an exile, and wandering back and forth? Who has brought these up? Behold, I was left alone. Where were these?’”

Thus says the Lord Yahweh, “Behold, I will lift up my hand to the nations, and lift up my banner to the peoples; and they shall bring your sons in their bosom, and your daughters shall be carried on their shoulders.

Kings shall be your foster fathers, and their queens your nursing mothers. They will bow down to you with their faces to the earth, and lick the dust of your feet; Then you will know that I am Yahweh; and those who wait for me shall not be disappointed.”
Shall the plunder be taken from the mighty, or the lawful captives be delivered?
But Yahweh says, “Even the captives of the mighty shall be taken away, and the plunder retrieved from the fierce; for I will contend with him who contends with you, and I will save your children.

I will feed those who oppress you with their own flesh; and they will be drunk on their own blood, as with sweet wine. Then all flesh shall know that I, Yahweh, am your Savior, and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.”

footnotes.content: Listen—a call that reaches from the womb to the islands. This servant was chosen before birth, named before breath. We're listening to the testimony of one called with a purpose older than time.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A sharp sword, a polished shaft—weapons of the Spirit. Hidden in His hand until the moment comes. The Lord prepares His messenger in secret, protecting the instrument of His word until it's time to strike.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Israel"—the very name speaks of struggle and grace. The servant is given the role of embodying God's glory, not through power but through obedience and faithfulness. This is how God chooses to be glorified: through a servant.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "I have labored in vain"—the honest lament of one who has poured everything out and seen no visible fruit. Yet even in this doubt, he knows where to find justice: not in results, but in the God who sees all labor and rewards all faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Formed in the womb for this very purpose—to gather scattered Israel home. There's something tender here: the one called to restore is told that being chosen itself makes him honorable, regardless of whether his work is welcomed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Too light a thing"—God expands the vision. What began as restoring one people becomes light to all nations, salvation to the ends of the earth. The humble calling grows into cosmic reach, yet it starts with the smallest act of faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Redeemer speaks to one despised by nations, whom rulers mock. Yet kings rise and worship at his name. This word inverts the world's order: shame becomes honor, rejection becomes recognition—all because the faithful God stands behind His chosen one.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: An acceptable time; a day of salvation. The servant becomes a covenant for the people—a bridge between God and man. He will raise up the land itself, restore what was lost, and give a heritage to those who had nothing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Come out!"—echoes of Lazarus, of every soul bound and darkened. The servant's first work is liberation: calling the captive to freedom, the lost to light. Then provision follows: green pastures for those who have known only stone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No hunger, no thirst, no scorching—the God of mercy leads like a shepherd leads. Every danger is warded; every need is met. This is the promise to those who have wandered long: the mercy of God never runs out, never slumbers.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Mountains become roads; highways are exalted. The barriers that divide become pathways for return. God remakes the geography of His people's restoration—every obstacle smoothed, every path made clear for the journey home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From afar, from north and west, from Sinim—the return is universal, from all corners. The scattering is reversed; what once fled in exile now rushes home. Geography speaks faith: wherever God's people are, they hear the call to return.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sing, heavens; be joyful, earth—all creation joins the song. God has comforted His people; compassion has moved Him. The cosmos itself celebrates because the heart of God toward the afflicted has not hardened but softened.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zion's cry: abandoned, forgotten. The pain is real, the feeling of abandonment is spoken aloud. The Lord does not silence this lament; instead, what follows shows it matters—He answers it with the deepest reassurance of His faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Could a mother forget her nursing child? The question is rhetorical, yet even then—"Yes, these may forget"—the Lord won't. His tenderness outstrips even the fierce love of a mother. He engraves us on His memory and His hands.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Engraved on the palms of His hands—the pierced hands of Christ. Zion's walls are constantly before the Lord's sight; we are not forgotten but inscribed, not absent but always in His gaze. This is the deepest comfort: we are remembered.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Your children hurry home; your destroyers depart. The reversal is swift once the Lord moves. Those who laid waste flee; those who were scattered hasten back. The tide turns because the God of hosts has spoken.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zion adorned like a bride, clothed with all her children as ornament—a picture of belonging and beauty restored. What was barren becomes fruitful; what was alone becomes surrounded. The Lord dresses His afflicted people in dignity.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Waste becomes too small for inhabitants; the land can't hold the returning multitude. What was desolate bursts with life. Those who consumed Zion are scattered far away—the tables turn completely when God decides it's time to restore.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Children cry, "This place is too small for me!" Abundance brings its own joy—too many blessings to contain, too much provision to fit. The widow's lament is swallowed by the noise of returned abundance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The astonished mother: "Who bore these for me?" Bereaved, alone, wandering—and suddenly surrounded by multitudes. The impossibility of it breaks her heart open; she can't account for such grace. Yet grace doesn't need accounting; it only asks acceptance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord lifts His hand and banner to the nations—a sign for all peoples to see. Nations themselves will carry Israel's children home as precious cargo. The kingdoms of the earth become servants of Israel's restoration.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Kings become foster fathers; queens, nursing mothers. The powerful bow and lick dust at the feet of the once-despised. Then will come knowledge: not intellectual but lived, felt, certain—that Yahweh is Redeemer, and those who wait on Him are not disappointed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Shall the plunder be taken from the mighty?" The question assumes the impossible. Yet it's asked to set up the answer: yes, even what the strong clutch is retrieved. No earthly power holds permanently against the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord says: even the mighty's captives will be freed; their plunder retrieved. He will contend with those who contend against His people, will save their children. His protection is absolute because His care is absolute.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "I will feed those who oppress you with their own flesh"—the judgment is severe, yet the chapter ends with recognition and redemption: all flesh knows that Yahweh is Savior and Redeemer. Today, readers echo this knowing: the Lord's arm is not shortened, and His covenant mercy remains.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
